line: Lenovo Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 (16" Intel, 2025)
config_name: Yoga Pro 9i Aura Edition Gen 10 — Core Ultra 7 255H, RTX 5050 8GB, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 16" 2.8K OLED 120Hz (base panel)

specs.keyboard_notes: Yoga creator keyboard; CNET noted slightly awkward keyboard placement

battery.notes: 84Wh (VERIFIED on lenovo.com/ca). Base 2.8K OLED slightly more efficient than 3.2K tandem.

price.notes: PDP lists both 2.8K OLED and 3.2K Tandem OLED panels (VERIFIED). ld+json price hidden (0); estimated ~US$1,630 x 1.35 from CNET anchor minus tandem-OLED uplift.

reviews.quote: Centered around a gorgeous 16-inch OLED display, this Yoga laptop provides the performance and build that graphics pros demand.
Six-speaker array produces tinny, hollow sound

praises: Cheapest way into the Pro 9i chassis: same 84Wh battery, RTX 5050 and aluminium build as the pricier tandem-OLED tier
2.8K OLED still covers 100% DCI-P3 with true blacks — plenty for photo editing
SD Express + HDMI + USB-A port set covers creator workflows without dongles
Noticeably quieter than the 3.2K tier under light loads since the panel draws less power
Frequently $200-300 off during Lenovo CA eCoupon events, making it the value creator pick
complaints: Base OLED lacks the tandem structure — HDR peaks dim faster than the 3.2K panel's sustained 1,600 nits
Glare coating on the base panel is worse in bright rooms than tandem tier's treatment
Six-speaker array sounds tinny on calls and video (CNET con)
Keyboard placement crowds the front edge (CNET con)

design_philosophy: The entry tier of Lenovo's 16-inch creator flagship keeps the full RTX 5050 + 32GB core spec and swaps only the panel to the standard 2.8K OLED, letting price-sensitive creators buy into the Pro 9i platform.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET's reviewed tandem-OLED config (8.6): panel swap to standard 2.8K OLED → screen_quality −1.0, readability_bright −1.0, battery +0.3. All other specs identical to anchor. CNET URL generic (exact slug unverified).
